title: CBIC Clarifies Adjudication of Customs Cases Involving Fraudulently Obtained DGFT Scrips
content:
# CBIC Clarifies Adjudication of Customs Cases Involving Fraudulently Obtained DGFT Scrips

Ek important update hai! Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) ne Customs cases ke adjudication ko lekar ek important instruction issue kiya hai, especially those involving fraudulently obtained DGFT scrips.

This Instruction (No. 17/2026-Cus) dated September 21, 2026, addresses difficulties faced by field formations where Show Cause Notices (SCNs) under Section 28AAA of the Customs Act, 1962, were pending because DGFT's cancellation of the relevant instrument or scrip was awaited.

Here are the key clarifications:

*   **When Customs/DRI alleges misdeclaration (e.g., misclassification, overvaluation) in the Shipping Bill:**
    *   Customs authorities should first investigate and adjudicate the matter under the Customs Act, 1962.
    *   Agar zaroorat ho, then consequential amendment to the Shipping Bill should be made.
    *   Only after this, the matter should be referred to DGFT for necessary action, including cancellation of the scrip. CBIC agrees with DGFT that scrips should not be cancelled solely based on allegations without a final customs determination.
*   **When allegations relate to policy interpretation, eligibility, or entitlement (DGFT's domain):**
    *   The matter must first be referred to DGFT, whose view on the validity and entitlement of the scrip will prevail.
*   **When DGFT cannot cancel a scrip (e.g., due to a court order):**
    *   SCNs issued under Section 28AAA need not remain pending. Adjudication authorities should proceed and decide such cases on merits.
*   **In other cases of alleged fraudulent procurement where DGFT has initiated cancellation proceedings:**
    *   Adjudication under Section 28AAA should take place *only after* DGFT cancels the instrument or scrip.

This clarification aims to streamline the adjudication process and reduce pendency in these complex cases.
